text.text_excerpt: i was here with a large group and they were more than willing to push tables together to accommodate our group. there were lots of paintings on the wall (probably local artists) and a guy pushed his bike through the dining area during our meal to apparently get to his room upstairs. J'Anitas definitely has some local flavor. i was drawn to this place because the menu was a bit different from the typical jambalaya/gumbo/etouffe standard "New Orleans" food. all the other reviews made the fish sammich sound really good, and i will have to agree, it was really good. i got mine with a side of Maque Choux and guacamole. the Maque Choux was somewhat new but good. it had corn, onions, tomatoes, a...

I love this place. I think they will be a great addition to the Rendon Inn. I recently went there on my way to the airport, for chicken friend steak... Kinda like a last meal on my way to the NW. Really really wonderful. the Mashers, and beans? good old skool southern yummy goodness. Of course, I had to have some guacamole, and some chips, because I'm addicted to them, and it had been a while. beer selection good, and I'm not really a beer drinker, but had a few, since we were on vacation. It was the perfect meal, and right amount of everything to send me on my way. I look forward to more meals at this place. Thank you Craig and Kimmee... again, you bring the goods!

If you were planning on trying a new restaurant tonight, just scrap it and head on over to the Rendon Inn. J'Anitas will make you forget all about your well thought out foodie excursion. This is bar food at its best. This is bar food that puts a lot of restaurant food to shame. There's nothing fancy about it. There's no table service so you have to order at the bar. The food is just appetizers and sandwiches served up in baskets. Make no mistake though, these sandwiches mean business. This isn't a ham and cheese or roast beef type of place.
